eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader consensus centers on 21–22°C as the most likely peak temperature for São Paulo on June 13, 2026, reflecting standard Southern Hemisphere winter conditions and recent model guidance.** 

June climatology places typical daily maxima near 21–23°C, with overnight lows around 13–15°C. A cold frontal passage on June 11–12 suppressed highs to the upper teens, but post-frontal stabilization and moderating northwest flow have allowed a modest rebound. Official forecasts from the Met Office, climate-data models, and extended outlooks consistently project a daytime high of 21–22°C under broken clouds with light showers possible, keeping values well below seasonal extremes. 

Higher outcomes (23°C+) carry low implied probability because no warm advection or clear-sky amplification is expected, while sub-20°C readings would require an unforecasted surge of cooler air. The tight clustering around 21–22°C captures the narrow uncertainty band in current numerical weather prediction runs ahead of final observations.

Recent model runs show modest warming potential from a building thermal trough, yet persistent stratus and sea breezes cap upside risk, pushing lower-probability outcomes for 78°F+ well below 20% combined. Historical analogs for mid-June heat intrusions support the current 57% implied probability for 74–77°F while underscoring how small shifts in 850 hPa temperatures or wind direction can swing the daily maximum by 3–5°F before evening.
